# ethereum-optimism/infra Weekly Report (Jul 19 - 25, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on hardening infrastructure security and advancing the decoupling of `op-geth` from core services. A major milestone was achieved in standardizing all infrastructure service Dockerfiles to Chainguard `wolfi-base` to minimize the attack surface. Significant progress was also made in refining the L2 transaction representation for the `op-batcher` migration and resolving complex race conditions in interop testing. The team successfully addressed long-standing parity issues between Kona-node and op-node, ensuring more robust safety mechanisms across the Superchain ecosystem.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Infrastructure Security and Standardization
The team prioritized security posture by migrating the entire infrastructure stack to more secure base images and remediating dependency vulnerabilities.
*   **Container Hardening:** All `infra` service Dockerfiles were standardized to use Chainguard `wolfi-base`, replacing legacy base images to improve maintainability and security ([#671](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/671)).
*   **Dependency Management:** A comprehensive update was performed across Go modules, Yarn workspaces, and Poetry projects to remediate flagged CVEs and ensure all dependencies are current ([#670](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/670)).

### op-geth Decoupling & L2 Representation
Work continued on the architectural shift to make `op-service/sources` the primary OP-aware Ethereum client, reducing direct dependencies on `op-geth` internals.
*   **Batcher Migration Strategy:** Design corrections were made for the `op-batcher` migration. It was determined that `op-batcher` will use `PayloadByNumber` to fetch `*eth.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` rather than `InfoAndUserTxs`, as the latter drops critical L1-info deposit and post-execution transactions required for batch building ([#20264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20264)).
*   **Transition Scaffolding:** Developers are utilizing `optypes` helpers (like `IsDepositTx`) as temporary scaffolding to decouple call sites from `op-geth` before the final L2 transaction representation changes are implemented ([#20263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20263)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Kona-node Parity:** The team resolved issues regarding `syncmode.offset-el-safe` for Kona-node, concluding that its existing safety mechanisms are more conservative than op-node and do not require the same bug-fix flags ([#21243](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21243)).
*   **Migration Tooling:** Super-root migration runbooks were updated to correctly reflect current fault-game behavior for simplified `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` configurations ([#21709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21709)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Interoperability Flakes:** A root cause was identified for `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`. The flake stems from a race condition where `FollowSource` canonicalizes a new block while a light sequencer timer is still armed against the previous parent. A fix involving mutex-protected parent header validation is currently being verified ([#21635](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21635)).
*   **Reth Integration Stability:** Investigation continues into a `SIGSEGV` in `reth-optimism-node` integration tests. While the "detached payload thread" hypothesis was refuted, the team is now looking into potential races between RocksDB background threads and C++ static destructors, with plans to capture core dumps in CI ([#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20973)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week's activity highlights a high degree of technical coordination regarding the `op-geth` decoupling project. Discussions between maintainers led to a significant pivot in how `op-batcher` handles transaction fetching, demonstrating a proactive approach to catching architectural regressions early. Collaboration is also evident in the cross-functional effort to standardize container images, which required updates across multiple package managers (Go, Yarn, Poetry) and service definitions. The deep-dive investigation into the `reth` integration flake shows a rigorous, evidence-based debugging culture, involving experimental verification and independent peer reviews of threading hypotheses.
